subject: FYI getNames overwritten by another package

messages.author: 43e2e19dd6bd2992
messages.subject: FYI getNames overwritten by another package
parts:
Hello all,

I am using another package that has a getNames object and overwrites
aroma.affymetrix's function. I know I can access the function myself
with aroma.affymetrix::getNames. But functions that call getNames are
not working, for example print. On a previous R list post someone said
that conflicting names shouldn't be a problem internally to a package if
the options are setup that deal with it, but I've lost the post
unfortunately... Or is this a problem that the OTHER package isn't
appropriately defining it's namespace or something, in which case I'll
contact that author?

Best,
Elizabeth

messages.author: 185f4d4fdb048fb8
messages.subject: Re: [aroma.affymetrix] FYI getNames overwritten by another package
parts:
Hi,

namespaces are supposed to handle this and I guess it might not have
been a problem if aroma.affymetrix had a namespace. Unfortunately it
is not straightforward to add a namespace to aroma.affymetrix. Last
time I tried it caused some side effects, but you are welcome to try
and see if it works.

Alternatively, if you load the "other" package before
aroma.affymetrix, then aroma.affymetrix will be ahead of the other
package on the search list and getNames() should be found as expected.
aroma.affymetrix defined getNames() as a generic function so the
other package should still work. In R.utils there is even the
moveInSearchPath() method that allows you to reorder the search() path
after loading the package. That might be handy as well.

Let us know if this solves your problem.

Henrik
